modelResponse.episodeSummary: 64F, Atrial Flutter with 1:1 AV conduction, critical severity, hemodynamically unstable (BP 88/54 mmHg)
keyECGEvidence: QRS duration 180 ms (widened from baseline 88 ms)
modelResponse.mechanism: Flecainide is a Class Ic antiarrhythmic that slows conduction velocity. In the setting of atrial flutter, it can paradoxically decrease the rate of the atrial circuit while simultaneously decreasing AV nodal conduction, leading to a dangerous 1:1 AV conduction ratio where the ventricular rate equals the atrial rate.
contributingFactors: Flecainide use without AV nodal blocker co-prescription
Recent initiation of flecainide (2 weeks ago)

rejectedAlternatives.why: Presence of visible flutter waves and 1:1 relationship between atrial and ventricular rates suggests a supraventricular origin; QRS widening is explained by flecainide and 1:1 conduction.
P-waves are absent and flutter waves are visible; rate of 200 bpm is too high for typical sinus rhythm in this context.

recommendedActions: Initiate AV nodal blockade (e.g., beta-blocker or calcium channel blocker) to increase AV nodal delay
Transfer to ICU/CCU for continuous cardiac monitoring
